newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES POLE POSITION.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES POLE POSITION.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve took pole position for Sunday's British Grand Prix at Silverstone after an exciting last-ditch bid in the closing minutes of Saturday's qualifying session.

The Canadian Williams driver, who trails German Michael Schumacher in the world drivers' championship by 14 points, had been unable to respond to the best time of Finland's Mika Hakkinen for much of the session before setting the fastest lap of one minute 21.598 seconds with just two minutes to go.
The pole position is the ninth of Villeneuve's career and leaves him favourite to secure his second consecutive victory in the British Grand Prix.
German Heinz-Harald Frentzen in the other Williams will start from second place on the grid after losing out to Villeneuve in the closing stages with a best time of one minute 21.732 seconds.

Hakkinen had dominated the practice sessions leading up to qualifying and spent much of the session in the pits while his time stayed top of the sheets. But he was unable to better Villeneuve's and Frentzen's times in the closing minutes.

Schumacher's best time of 1:21.977 was enough for fourth on the grid but the nature of the Silverstone track will make it difficult for the double world champion to challenge for the lead in Sunday's 60-lap race.
